backlog.spec: After the first SLSQP run, keep the best packing and repeatedly perturb it: add Gaussian noise (sigma about 0.02) to all centres and radii, clip centres into the square, re-run SLSQP from that point, and accept the result only if its repaired radius sum improves. Continue until the time budget is used. Use rng from the seed for every perturbation.
backlog.title: Basin hopping from the incumbent

backlog.spec: Starting from the best packing, remove the circle with the smallest radius, sample about 2000 random candidate points in the square, place the circle at the candidate whose distance to the nearest other circle minus its radius is largest, then re-run SLSQP on the full set. Accept if the repaired sum improves, otherwise keep the previous best.
backlog.title: Remove-and-reinsert the smallest circle

backlog.spec: Pass a jac argument to minimize that returns the exact gradient of the objective and of the constraint vector (pair distance terms, wall terms and radius non-negativity). Build the sparse pair Jacobian with the same index arrays iu used by cons. This removes finite-difference cost so each SLSQP iteration is much cheaper, which yields more restarts in the time budget.
backlog.title: Analytic Jacobians for SLSQP

backlog.spec: Only include pair constraints for pairs whose centre distance is below a cutoff (for example the sum of current radii plus 0.15) when the problem is set up, rebuilding the list after each SLSQP call. Full pair sets are O(n^2) constraints of which most are slack. Keep the wall and non-negativity constraints for all circles. Verify the final repaired packing still checks every pair.
backlog.title: Neighbour-list pair constraints

backlog.spec: Phase 1: minimise a quadratic overlap penalty sum(max(0, r_i+r_j-d_ij)^2) plus wall penalties minus lambda times the radius sum with L-BFGS-B, increasing lambda geometrically over about 5 stages. Phase 2: feed the resulting centres and radii into the existing SLSQP call as the starting point. The penalty stage gives a feasible-ish start that SLSQP can polish quickly.
backlog.title: Penalty continuation before SLSQP

backlog.spec: After SLSQP and clipping, freeze the centres and solve a linear program with scipy.optimize.linprog that maximises the sum of radii subject to linearised non-overlap constraints r_i + r_j <= d_ij (using current distances) and wall bounds r_i <= the distance to each wall. Iterate the LP a few times, re-linearising at the new centres, then apply the existing repair. This replaces the crude shrink step with an optimal radius assignment.
backlog.title: LP polish of radii with fixed centres

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call with scipy.optimize.minimize using method trust-constr, passing the same objective and the NonlinearConstraint with lower bound 0 and upper bound infinity built from cons. Keep the time check and repair unchanged. Compare the best repaired sum against the SLSQP version within the same time budget and keep whichever construction is used consistently.
backlog.title: trust-constr instead of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Maintain an elite pool of the best 5 packings found so far, deduplicated by sorted radii. Each new start is either a fresh random init (probability 0.3) or a child made by taking the centres of one elite parent for the circles in one half of the square and the centres of another parent for the other half, then fixing the circle count by moving surplus circles to random positions. Run SLSQP on each child and insert the result into the pool.
backlog.title: Elite memetic recombination

backlog.spec: With probability 0.5 per restart, generate an initial configuration that is symmetric about the vertical line x = 0.5 or the diagonal: sample ceil(n/2) centres in one half, mirror them to fill the rest, and drop the extra circle at a random point if n is odd. Start SLSQP from that configuration. Mix these with the existing uniform random inits and keep the best result overall.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric initialisation

backlog.spec: Generate starts from a perturbed square or hexagonal lattice: choose a random lattice orientation near 0 or 30 degrees and random spacing so that about n points fall in the unit square, select n points, add uniform jitter of size 0.03 and clip into [0.05, 0.95]. Use these as the x0 centres with radii set to 0.05, alongside the existing uniform random inits.
backlog.title: Lattice-perturbed initialisation

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform draw of initial centres with a Latin hypercube sample in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2: split each axis into n equal strata, permute strata independently for x and y using rng, and draw one point per stratum cell. This spreads the starting circles more evenly, which usually gives SLSQP better-separated starts and fewer early collisions.
backlog.title: Latin hypercube centre sampling

backlog.spec: Change INIT_LOW from 0.1 to 0.0 so the initial centres range over the whole unit square, and sample radii uniformly in [0.01, 0.1] rather than fixing them at 0.05. Wider starts explore more of the configuration space across restarts. The clipping and repair steps already keep the final packing valid.
backlog.title: Widen the init box to the full square

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.93 so that the restart loop uses most of the 30 s CPU budget. The process_time check still stops the loop before the 45 s hard limit because the final repair takes only milliseconds. Leave all other logic unchanged so the gain comes purely from additional restarts.
backlog.title: Use more of the time budget

backlog.spec: Run the first few restarts with MAX_ITER set to 100 to rank starts cheaply, then re-run only the top 3 candidates with MAX_ITER set to 1000 and a tighter ftol of 1e-12. This spends the expensive long optimisation only on promising basins while keeping broad early exploration.
backlog.title: Adaptive SLSQP iteration cap

backlog.spec: Inside a basin-hopping loop started from the best packing, scale the perturbation sigma geometrically from 0.05 down to 0.002 over the remaining time budget, so early moves explore widely and late moves refine locally. Accept a new packing when its repaired radius sum is larger than the current one, and track the global best separately.
backlog.title: Annealed basin-hopping noise

backlog.spec: Phase 1: run SLSQP with all radii tied to a single shared variable t, maximising t subject to the packing constraints, which gives a well-spread equal-circle arrangement. Phase 2: release the radii to independent variables and run the existing SLSQP call from that state. The equal-radius phase avoids the poor local optima that independent radii often fall into early.
backlog.title: Two-phase equal-radius start

backlog.spec: Optimise the weighted objective minus sum of w_i r_i, where w_i starts at 1 plus a random perturbation and is annealed toward 1 over two SLSQP calls. The weights bias the early optimisation toward different size distributions, after which the true unweighted sum objective is restored for the final polish. Keep the final repair and best-tracking unchanged.
backlog.title: Radius-weighted objective annealing

backlog.spec: Replace the iterative max-overlap shrink in _repair with a single global scaling step: compute the minimum over all pairs of d_ij divided by (r_i + r_j) and the minimum wall margin ratio, scale all radii by the smaller of these ratios, then subtract SHRINK. This keeps the relative radius profile found by SLSQP instead of shrinking only the worst pair, and it is simpler to reason about.
backlog.title: Exact overlap-resolving repair

backlog.spec: From the best packing, pick two circles whose radii differ by more than 0.05 and swap their radii while keeping their centres, then re-run SLSQP from that state. Repeat with random pairs for a fixed number of attempts per restart. Swapping radii changes which positions host large circles, a move that random perturbation rarely produces.
backlog.title: Swap radii of mismatched circles

backlog.spec: Solve the problem for n minus 1 circles with a short SLSQP run, then insert the new circle at the largest empty spot found by sampling 2000 candidate points, set its radius to the largest feasible value at that point, and re-run SLSQP for n circles. Use this grown start in addition to random restarts, keeping whichever final packing has the largest repaired radius sum.
backlog.title: Grow from a smaller packing

backlog.spec: Add a small term -lambda * sum over pairs of log(d_ij) (with lambda about 1e-3) to the SLSQP objective during the first SLSQP call only, which discourages circles from collapsing together and pushes the start toward a well-spread configuration. Drop the term for the final polish so the reported objective is the true radius sum.
backlog.title: Soft spread regulariser

backlog.spec: Add a penalty of -mu * sum(log(r_i + 1e-3)) to the objective with mu decaying from 1e-2 to 0 across the SLSQP iterations of a single call, which keeps small circles from vanishing too early and lets the optimiser move them. Finish with an unregularised SLSQP call so the returned radii are optimal for the true objective.
backlog.title: Radius floor regularisation

backlog.spec: Generate a batch of 200 random starts at once, score each with a cheap feasibility-based estimate (for example the sum of radii obtained from the nearest-neighbour bound min(wall distance, half the nearest centre distance) using numpy broadcasting), and run full SLSQP only on the top 10 percent. This spends the expensive optimisation on the most promising starts without changing the optimiser.
backlog.title: Vectorised pre-screening of starts

backlog.spec: From the best packing, choose a random subset of about 12 circles that are spatially close to a random point, freeze all others, and run SLSQP only over the chosen subset with the frozen circles as fixed obstacles. Accept the result if the full repaired radius sum improves. Repeat with new random subsets for the time budget. Smaller subproblems solve faster and explore local rearrangements.
backlog.title: Random subset re-optimisation

backlog.spec: Start SLSQP with the wall constraints tightened so that circles must lie within [0.02, 0.98] squared, then relax the margin to zero in a second SLSQP call from the first result. The tightened stage keeps circles away from edges while the packing arranges itself, and the relaxed stage lets edge circles grow to their final size.
backlog.title: Gradual wall-margin relaxation

backlog.spec: Optimise under a prescribed symmetry, then unfold. Pick one symmetry at random per call from {reflection in the diagonal x=y, 180-degree rotation about (0.5,0.5)}, seeded by rng. Parameterise only ceil(n/2) free circles plus their images, with the self-symmetric circles (on the axis or centre) handled by fixing them to the symmetry set. Run SLSQP on the reduced variables (about half the constraints), which is much faster and explores a different region. Then unfold to all n circles, run one unconstrained SLSQP polish from that configuration, and keep the best of the symmetric and polished results in the basin-hopping loop.
backlog.title: Symmetry-reduced search

backlog.spec: Replace the random SLSQP start with an event-free compression. Start with n points at random positions with tiny radii. Repeat: grow every radius by a factor (1 + g), then push overlapping pairs and wall-violating circles apart with a few vectorised gradient steps on the squared overlap energy, using a shrinking step. When overlap energy cannot be driven to near zero, reduce g by half and add a small random jitter to centres. Stop when g falls below 1e-6. Use the resulting jammed packing as the start for the existing SLSQP and basin-hopping stages. Everything is numpy, with the seed controlling all randomness.
backlog.title: Lubachevsky-Stillinger-style growth compression

backlog.spec: Initialise centres with best-candidate (Mitchell) Poisson-disk sampling instead of uniform random points. For each new centre, draw k=30 candidates uniformly in [0,1]^2 and keep the one farthest from all existing centres. Use this for the first SLSQP start in _solve_once, with radii set to the distance to the nearest centre or wall times 0.5. Leave the basin-hopping stage unchanged. This gives evenly spread starts that avoid the clustered configurations uniform sampling produces.
backlog.title: Blue-noise Poisson-disk initialisation

backlog.spec: Build a start by placing circles one at a time in decreasing order of target radius, where the target radii follow a random decreasing profile drawn from rng. For each circle, find the point in a 200x200 grid that maximises the distance to existing centres and walls (the largest empty hole), place the circle there with radius equal to the minimum of that clearance and its target, and continue. Feed the resulting centres and radii as x0 to SLSQP. This replaces the uniform random start only, and costs well under a second for n=32.
backlog.title: Greedy largest-hole sequential placement

backlog.spec: Run K=4 basin-hopping chains in lockstep, each at a different temperature T in a geometric ladder from 0.0005 to 0.01. Each chain proposes a perturbed, SLSQP-relaxed, repaired packing and accepts it with the Metropolis rule on the sum of radii (accept if the new sum is larger, otherwise with probability exp(delta/T)). After each sweep, attempt swaps between neighbouring temperatures with the standard replica-exchange probability. Return the best packing seen by any chain. Keep the time budget and the perturbation scale unchanged.
backlog.title: Replica-exchange basin hopping

backlog.spec: Remove the radius variables from the optimisation. Define each radius as a function of the centres: r_i = softmin over the wall distances and the half-gaps (d_ij - r_j) with a temperature beta, using log-sum-exp with beta annealed from 30 to 300. Maximise the sum of these radii with L-BFGS-B on the 2n centre coordinates, using a numerical or analytic gradient. Finish with the existing SLSQP call starting from the resulting centres and radii. This cuts the variable count from 3n to 2n and removes the pairwise constraint matrix from the early stages.
backlog.title: Smooth-min radius reparameterisation

backlog.spec: Add a barrier term to the objective during the SLSQP stage in place of the hard overlap constraints alone. The objective becomes minus the sum of radii minus mu times the sum of log(slack) over all pair and wall slacks, with mu annealed from 1e-2 to 1e-6 across the stage. Each log term is evaluated only where the slack is positive, and a large penalty is used otherwise. Perform one final SLSQP solve with the hard constraints and mu=0, starting from the barrier solution. This keeps circles away from degenerate touching configurations early on and should reduce the amount the repair step has to shrink.
backlog.title: Log-barrier contact regularisation

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, identify rattlers: circles with fewer than two active contacts (pair or wall, within 1e-7 of zero slack). Remove the smallest rattler, search a 200x200 grid for the point with the largest clearance to other centres and walls, and move that circle there with radius set to the clearance. Re-run SLSQP from this configuration. Apply this move only with probability 0.3 inside the basin-hopping loop, so the step remains a targeted rearrangement rather than a full restart.
backlog.title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: Generate starts by solving a larger problem. Call _solve_once with n+1 circles from the random start, then delete the circle with the smallest radius and re-optimise the remaining n circles from the resulting centres and radii with SLSQP. Use this as a new start source with probability 0.5 at each restart, and keep the existing basin-hopping loop for the rest of the time. The idea is that a dense packing of n+1 circles sheds a circle into a configuration that is a good start for n.
backlog.title: Shrink from n+1 circles

backlog.spec: Allocate the time budget across many starts in rounds. Round 1 draws 40 random starts and runs SLSQP with maxiter=25 on each, keeping the top 10 by sum of repaired radii. Round 2 runs maxiter=80 on the top 10 and keeps the top 3. Round 3 gives the top 3 the full MAX_ITER budget and then uses the remaining time for basin hopping from the best. Stop each stage by the process-time clock so the total stays within TIME_FRACTION. This replaces the fixed-budget random restarts with a bracket that spends most compute on promising basins.
backlog.title: Successive-halving over starts

backlog.spec: Keep the basin-hopping loop, but count consecutive steps without improvement of best. If the count reaches K=25 (sum of radii not improved by more than 1e-6), discard the incumbent and restart from a fresh random SLSQP solve from _solve_once(n, rng), storing it as the new incumbent only if it is better than the old best. Otherwise continue basin hopping from the current best. Reset the counter after any restart or improvement. Use the same time check and repair step as now.
backlog.title: Stagnation-triggered fresh restart

backlog.spec: Replace the greedy accept rule (accept only if r.sum() > best sum) with threshold accepting. Maintain a current solution cur separate from the global best. Accept a candidate into cur if its repaired sum is greater than cur's sum minus a threshold T, where T decreases linearly from 0.01 at the start of the loop to 0 at the time limit, measured by elapsed process time over TIME_FRACTION*time_limit. Always update the global best when a candidate beats it. Perturbation and SLSQP solve stay as they are.
backlog.title: Threshold-accepting basin hopping

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, add a quadratic proximal penalty to the SLSQP objective: minimise -sum(r) + lam * ||c - c0||^2 + lam * ||r - r0||^2, where c0, r0 are the perturbed start and lam = 0.5. This keeps each local solve near its starting basin rather than letting it drift to a distant one. Use the same constraints. After this solve, run one unpenalised SLSQP pass starting from the penalised result (maxiter MAX_ITER) to recover the true optimum, then repair as before.
backlog.title: Proximal-anchored SLSQP in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For each SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop, draw a random margin m uniformly in [0, 0.003] and tighten all non-overlap constraints to d_ij - r_i - r_j - m >= 0 and all wall constraints to margin m as well. The tightened problem pushes the optimiser into interior configurations with slack, which can escape jammed states. Run the final SLSQP pass with m=0 from that result so the returned solution satisfies the true constraints. Use the seed-driven rng for m.
backlog.title: Randomised constraint tightening during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a small regularisation term to the SLSQP objective: minus sum(r) minus eps * sum(r*(1-r)) where eps = 1e-3 is fixed, or alternatively a term that penalises the variance of radii with weight 1e-3. The aim is to favour configurations where radii are not all equal, so the search explores more varied size distributions. After the regularised solve, run a plain SLSQP pass with the true objective (no regularisation) from its output and keep whichever packing has the larger true radius sum after repair.
backlog.title: Small-radius diversity bonus

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP initial solve with a hard-disk Monte Carlo compression. Start with n random centres and radii 0.001. Repeat for 2000 sweeps: propose a random displacement of each centre by a Gaussian step of size 0.05 times the current step scale, accept only if the circle stays inside the square and does not overlap any other circle given current radii, then try to grow each radius to the maximum allowed by its nearest neighbours and the walls, times 0.999 plus a small random factor. Reduce the step scale by a factor 0.99 every 50 sweeps. Pass the resulting centres and radii into SLSQP as the start. All randomness uses rng.
backlog.title: Hard-disk Monte Carlo compression start

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random centres in _solve_once with a ring-shell layout. Place roughly 4 sqrt(n) circles evenly on the boundary perimeter inset by about 0.05, with an angular offset drawn from rng. Fill the remaining circles uniformly at random in the interior [0.15, 0.85]^2. Start radii at INIT_RADIUS. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Use rng for all draws so that the seed controls the layout.
backlog.title: Ring-shell initialisation

backlog.spec: Add a move type to basin hopping. With probability 0.5, split the square into four quadrants around a random point (cx, cy) drawn in [0.35, 0.65]^2. Pick one quadrant at random. Take the circles whose centres lie inside it and solve a sub-problem with SLSQP on just those circles, keeping the other circles fixed as obstacles (add their non-overlap constraints as constants in the constraint function). Accept the sub-solution into the full configuration if the total radius sum improves after repair. Otherwise fall back to the existing full-SLSQP perturbation step.
backlog.title: Quadrant domain-decomposition moves

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve, run a short augmented Lagrangian loop. Use L-BFGS-B on the bounded variables (centres in [0,1], radii in [0,0.5]) to minimise -sum(r) plus, for every constraint g_k >= 0 (pair overlaps and wall margins), the term (mu/2) * (max(0, lam_k - mu*g_k))^2 - lam_k^2/(2 mu), with lam_k as multipliers. After each inner solve, update lam_k = max(0, lam_k - mu*g_k) and increase mu by 2 for up to 5 outer iterations. Pass the output to the existing SLSQP solve as the starting point. This replaces the fixed-weight penalty idea by using multiplier updates.
backlog.title: Augmented-Lagrangian pre-solve with L-BFGS-B

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform Gaussian perturbation in basin hopping with a targeted one. Compute the contact graph of the incumbent: circles i and j are in contact if their gap is below 1e-4, and wall contact if a circle touches a wall within 1e-4. Identify rattlers as circles with fewer than 2 contacts. With probability 0.5, perturb only the rattlers and their neighbours with sigma 0.05, leaving the rest of the configuration fixed. Otherwise use the existing global Gaussian perturbation. Keep all other steps and the acceptance rule unchanged.
backlog.title: Contact-graph-guided perturbation

backlog.spec: Inside solve, for the first ~25% of the time budget, split the n circles into two groups (sizes n//2 and n - n//2). Run _solve_once independently on each group inside its own sub-square: a unit square scaled to half width, placed left and right (or top and bottom, chosen randomly from rng). Map the two sub-packings back to the unit square, scale radii by the same factor, and run _solve_once on the full set starting from the concatenated result with radii clipped to the walls. Use this merged solution as the initial incumbent for the existing basin-hopping loop. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Two-cluster hierarchical merge

backlog.spec: Replace the global Gaussian perturbation in the basin-hopping loop with a local one. With probability 0.5 each step, pick a random circle, take its k=4 nearest neighbours (by centre distance), and redraw only those five centres uniformly inside the square, keeping their radii shrunk by 0.5. Otherwise use the existing global perturbation. Feed the result to _solve_once with the same repair. Accept the move only if the repaired radius sum improves on the incumbent, as before.
backlog.title: Local cluster shake move

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, draw centres not uniformly but by rejection sampling against a density that is low near existing centres. For each new centre, draw 30 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 and keep the one whose distance to the nearest already-placed centre is largest (a best-candidate step). This is a cheap spread-out start. Keep the radii initialised at INIT_RADIUS and leave the SLSQP call and repair unchanged. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Density-matched rejection initialisation

backlog.spec: Track the success rate of basin-hopping steps over a sliding window of 20 steps. Start the Gaussian perturbation sigma at 0.02. Every 20 steps, multiply sigma by 1.2 if more than 1/5 of the steps improved the incumbent, and by 0.85 otherwise. Clamp sigma to [0.001, 0.1]. Apply the same sigma to both centre and radius noise. This replaces any fixed noise scale and needs no time-based schedule.
backlog.title: One-fifth-rule adaptive perturbation size

backlog.spec: After the final incumbent is chosen, identify the active contacts: pairs whose gap is below 1e-7 and walls where a circle touches the boundary within 1e-7. Form the system of equalities for these active constraints in the variables (centres, radii). Solve it with a few Gauss-Newton steps (least-squares via numpy.linalg.lstsq on the Jacobian of the active constraints) starting from the incumbent, keeping only steps that increase the radius sum and leave all non-active constraints satisfied. Finish with _repair so the packing is valid to 1e-10. Skip the polish if the system is rank-deficient or no step improves the sum.
backlog.title: Active-set Newton polish

backlog.spec: Maintain a running mean of the successful perturbation vectors in basin hopping. When a step improves the incumbent, add its perturbation delta to an exponentially weighted average (weight 0.2) and use this averaged direction, normalised and scaled by sigma, as the mean shift for the next proposals. Mix it with isotropic noise: proposal = incumbent + sigma * (0.5 * unit_mean_dir + 0.5 * gaussian). Keep sigma fixed at 0.02. The idea is to take larger steps along directions that have recently helped. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Learned perturbation direction (CMA-style)

backlog.spec: During each SLSQP call inside the basin-hopping loop, replace the objective -sum(r) with -sum(w_i * r_i), where the weights w_i are drawn once per call from uniform[0.9, 1.1] using the seeded rng. This breaks symmetry between circles and lets SLSQP reach different vertices of the feasible set. Constraints are unchanged. Score every candidate with the true unweighted radius sum after _repair, and keep the usual acceptance rule. Keep the first start unweighted.
backlog.title: Random per-circle objective weight jitter

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, solve the packing in a container of side s drawn uniformly from [0.97, 1.03] instead of 1, by changing the wall constraints in _solve_once to use s. Rescale the resulting centres by 1/s so they fit the unit square, rescale radii by 1/s, then clip centres to [0, 1] and run _repair. Accept by the usual rule. The perturbation nudges the solution across the wall boundary and may move circles into new contact patterns. Use only the seeded rng.
backlog.title: Container scale jitter

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop, pick the circle with the smallest radius and try 30 random new centres for it, uniform in the square. For each trial, compute the local score: the sum of radii of that circle and its neighbours, after setting its radius to the largest value that fits without overlap with the rest of the packing (use the min of wall distance and gap to the nearest circle). Keep the best trial, then run _solve_once starting from that configuration. This makes a targeted move and avoids a fully random restart of the circle.
backlog.title: Greedy relocation sweep with local evaluation

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, generate the 2n centre coordinates from a Halton sequence in base 2 and base 3 (two dimensions) instead of rng.uniform. Use a random integer offset drawn from rng so each seed gives a different subsequence, then scale the points to [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Keep the radii at INIT_RADIUS and leave everything else unchanged. Halton points cover the square more evenly than pseudo-random ones, which may give better basins for the first start.
backlog.title: Quasi-random Halton centre initialisation

backlog.spec: Inside the basin-hopping loop, with probability 0.3 per step, pick a random circle that touches a wall (within 1e-6 of an edge). Slide its centre along that wall to a uniform random position on the wall, keeping its radius, and then run the existing relocate-free SLSQP solve on the result. Otherwise keep the current perturbation. This is one extra branch in the loop and uses only numpy.
backlog.title: Wall-slide move in basin hopping

backlog.spec: For each basin-hopping step, run a cheap SLSQP with maxiter 25 from the perturbed start and compute its repaired sum of radii. Only if that screened sum is within 0.01 of the incumbent's sum, run the full SLSQP with MAX_ITER 200 from the same start and accept it if it improves the incumbent. This spends the 30 s budget on more candidates, with the expensive solve reserved for plausible ones.
backlog.title: Two-stage screening of basin-hopping candidates

backlog.spec: Change the pair constraint to d_ij - r_i - r_j - MARGIN >= 0 with MARGIN = 1e-7, and the wall constraints to use the same margin. SLSQP's tolerance then tends to land slightly inside the feasible set, so _repair shrinks less and the repaired sum keeps more of the optimiser's value. Keep SHRINK at 1e-9 and check the harness tolerance is still met.
backlog.title: Feasibility margin in the SLSQP pair constraints

backlog.spec: Remove the four wall-constraint blocks from cons() (the x-r, y-r, 1-x-r, 1-y-r terms) and pass the box limits through SLSQP's bounds argument: centres in [0, 1] and radii in [0, 0.5]. Keep the r >= 0 and pair constraints as they are. This shrinks the constraint matrix by about 4n rows, which should give SLSQP more iterations within the time limit.
backlog.title: Native box bounds instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: In each basin-hopping step, take the 25 percent largest-radius circles of the incumbent and hold their centres fixed while the rest are perturbed and solved with SLSQP, using a reduced problem over the other circles with the fixed ones included as constants in the pair constraints. Then run one full SLSQP over all circles from that result, accepting it only if its repaired sum improves the incumbent. This focuses the search on the loose part of the packing.
backlog.title: Frozen-core perturbation stage

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, choose a random point p in the square and a radius R uniformly between 0.2 and 0.35. Rotate the centres of all circles within distance R of p about p by a random angle in [-pi/3, pi/3], keep only rotated centres inside the square (clip them), and then run the usual SLSQP. This is a larger structured move than Gaussian noise and can reorder a local region of the packing.
backlog.title: Sub-disk rotation kick

backlog.spec: When comparing a candidate with the incumbent, accept it when its repaired sum is larger, or when the sums differ by less than 1e-5 and its smallest radius is larger. This lexicographic rule lets the search move along flat directions of the sum toward packings with more evenly sized circles, which can open room for later improvements. It changes only the acceptance comparison.
backlog.title: Secondary max-min radius tie-break

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with a quasi-random Halton sequence of 2n points in [0.05, 0.95]^2, scrambled by a random shift taken from the seed, and place the first four centres at the corners (0.05, 0.05), (0.95, 0.05), (0.05, 0.95), (0.95, 0.95). Initial radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Only the start changes; the rest of the pipeline stays the same.
backlog.title: Corner-anchored initial layout with Halton centres

backlog.spec: Track the number of basin-hopping steps since the incumbent last improved. If that count exceeds 40, replace the chain's current solution with a fresh random SLSQP start, keep the global best as it is, and reset the counter. The global best is only replaced when a candidate beats it. This gives the search a diversified restart when it stalls, without discarding the best packing found.
backlog.title: Reheated restart after stagnation

backlog.spec: Within _relocate, weight the smallest circle's candidate score by the number of contacts it would make, counting a contact as a neighbour within 1e-3 of touching, and add a bonus of 0.5 times that count to the score. Draw the candidate centre from a random point that lies in the largest empty region found from 200 uniform samples, using the existing trials loop. This favours moves that place the smallest circle where it wedges between existing ones.
backlog.title: Rattler-aware relocation weights

backlog.spec: Replace the SLSQP call inside _solve_once with a sequential linear programming loop. At each iterate (c, r), linearise every pair-distance constraint, the wall constraints and the radius bounds, then solve the LP max sum(dr) using scipy.optimize.linprog(method='highs') over the step (dc, dr) with box trust-region bounds |dc|, |dr| <= delta. Accept the step if the true constraint violation shrinks and the objective rises, otherwise halve delta. Stop when delta < 1e-7 or after 60 iterations. Restrict the pair constraints to pairs closer than 2*(r_i+r_j)+0.1 to keep the LP small. The LP vertex solutions should land exactly on the active contacts, which SLSQP often leaves slightly loose. Keep the basin-hopping loop and _repair unchanged.
backlog.title: Sequential LP trust-region polish

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, instead of isotropic Gaussian noise on the incumbent, build the Hessian of a penalty energy E(c,r) = -sum(r) + mu * sum(max(0, overlap)^2 + max(0, wall violation)^2) at the incumbent, using finite differences of the analytic gradient or a numerical Hessian (dimension 3n = 96, cheap). Take the eigenvectors with the 5 smallest non-zero eigenvalues (the floppy modes) and displace the incumbent along a random combination of them with amplitude drawn from U[0.01, 0.05], then clip to the square. Use the Gaussian kick with probability 0.5 and this soft-mode kick otherwise. Pass the perturbed point to _solve_once as the warm start, with everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Soft-mode Hessian perturbation kick

backlog.spec: Replace the random multi-start with a population-based search. Keep a population of 40 candidate packings encoded as 3n-vectors (centres plus radii). Each generation, form a trial vector with DE/rand/1/bin (F=0.6, CR=0.9) and score it by a penalised objective: sum of radii after the greedy repair of _repair. Keep the top 8 members after each generation and polish only the best candidate with _solve_once as a warm start. Loop until 80 percent of the CPU budget is used, then return the best polished packing. Vectorise the repair and scoring over the population where possible so that a generation takes well under 0.1 s for n=32.
backlog.title: Differential evolution over centres with SLSQP polish

backlog.spec: Define four basin-hopping moves: Gaussian kick (sigma 0.02), relocate-smallest (existing _relocate), a local cluster shake of five neighbouring circles, and a wall-slide that moves one boundary circle along its wall by U[-0.1,0.1]. Keep a success score per move, initialised at 1. Choose the move each step with probability proportional to its score plus 0.2 as an exploration floor. After each step, add 1 to the score of the move if it improved the incumbent and multiply all scores by 0.99 to forget old results. Log nothing and keep the code under 25 added lines.
backlog.title: Adaptive operator selection over perturbation moves

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation applied before the SLSQP solve in the basin-hopping loop. Sample 4000 random points in the unit square and assign each to the nearest centre under the power (radically weighted) distance d(p,c_i)^2 - r_i^2. Move each centre to the centroid of its assigned points, blended with its current position at weight 0.5, for 3 iterations. This pushes the packing toward a power-diagram centroidal state and removes local bias before the SLSQP solve. Apply this move with probability 0.3 per step, otherwise use the existing kick. Seed the sampling from the rng argument.
backlog.title: Lloyd centroidal relaxation kick

backlog.spec: Modify _relocate so it avoids moving circles that were relocated in the last 5 basin-hopping steps. Maintain a deque of recently moved indices and exclude them from the candidate set when choosing k = argmin(r). If all small circles are tabu, pick the smallest non-tabu circle instead. Also, when a step is rejected (the new packing does not beat the incumbent), record the moved index in the tabu list anyway so the search keeps cycling through different circles. Keep the rest of the loop unchanged.
backlog.title: Tabu-protected relocation

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping kick, scale the Gaussian noise per circle by its contact count instead of using a uniform sigma. Compute contacts from the incumbent as pairs with centre distance less than r_i + r_j + 1e-3, plus wall contacts where any side is within 1e-3 of the wall. Set sigma_i = 0.03 for circles with 0 or 1 contacts (likely rattlers, which should move freely) and sigma_i = 0.01 for circles with 4 or more contacts (rigid core, which should move little). Use 0.02 otherwise. Apply the same per-circle sigma to the radius noise. Everything else in the loop stays the same.
backlog.title: Contact-count-scaled perturbation noise

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP multi-start, run scipy.optimize.dual_annealing on the penalised energy E(c,r) = -sum(r) + mu * (sum of squared pair overlaps + squared wall violations), with mu = 100, over bounds [0,1] for centres and [0,0.5] for radii. Pass the rng-derived seed as seed and set maxfun so the call uses about 25 percent of the CPU budget. Use the best point as the warm start for _solve_once and then continue with the basin hopping loop unchanged. This tests whether a global annealer finds a better basin than random starts for n=32.
backlog.title: Dual annealing global search on penalty energy

backlog.spec: Add a topology move to the basin-hopping step with probability 0.2. Choose a random pair of circles whose centres are within 2.5 times the mean radius of each other, delete both, and insert one circle at their midpoint with radius equal to the sum of their radii times 0.8 (clipped to the wall limits). Then reinsert a circle at the centre of the largest empty region found by sampling 500 random points, with radius equal to the distance to the nearest circle or wall. Run SLSQP on the modified packing, which has n circles again, and accept it only if the repaired sum of radii beats the incumbent.
backlog.title: Merge-and-split topology move

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP polish in the basin-hopping loop, run a short coordinate pattern search on the repaired packing. For 40 iterations, pick a random circle and a random axis, try moving that centre coordinate by +step and -step with step starting at 0.01 and halving on failure, and accept a move only if _repair of the new packing has a larger sum of radii. Stop early when step < 1e-4. This is derivative-free and only accepts strict improvements, so it cannot reduce the score. It targets the small residual gap between the SLSQP optimum and the published 2.9370 value.
backlog.title: Pattern search over centre coordinates

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, draw the initial radii from a sorted power-law profile instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS: r_sorted = 0.02 + 0.06 * (1 - k/n)**2 for k = 0..n-1, then permute them randomly with rng.permutation. Place the largest starting radii on the centres nearest the middle of the square by sorting the uniform centre samples by distance to (0.5, 0.5) before assigning radii. Keep everything else unchanged, so SLSQP and the repair step are untouched.
backlog.title: Power-law radius prior for the first start

backlog.spec: In solve, after the first _solve_once, replace the radius perturbation r0 = br + N(0, 0.02) by a gap-based initialisation for each perturbed centre set: for every circle compute the distance to its nearest other centre and to the four walls, set r_i = 0.5 * min(nearest-neighbour distance, 2 * wall distance) * U(0.8, 1.0) with the same rng, then pass these as the radii to _relocate and _solve_once. Use this only on a random half of the basin-hopping steps, so the incumbent's radii still get used otherwise.
backlog.title: Nearest-neighbour gap radii for the basin-hopping start

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, optimise over s = log(r) instead of r, so the non-negativity of radii is automatic and the 'r >= 0' inequality rows disappear. The pair and wall constraints become cons(v) with r = exp(v[2n:]), and the objective is -exp(v[2n:]).sum(). Start from s0 = log(max(r0, 1e-3)). Convert back to radii with exp before returning. Keep the same iteration cap, the same wall and pair constraints, and the same repair step.
backlog.title: Log-radius reparameterisation of SLSQP

backlog.spec: Add a discrete pre-stage that is used only for the very first start. Build a 30 by 30 grid of candidate centres inside [0.05, 0.95]^2 and a fixed set of radius levels. Start with n occupied sites chosen at random. Run simulated annealing for about 3000 moves: each move relocates one occupied site to a random empty site, and the score is the sum of greedy radii, where each occupied site's radius is min(wall distance, half the distance to its nearest occupied neighbour). Accept with the Metropolis rule at a temperature that falls linearly from 0.01 to 0. Feed the best occupancy's centres and greedy radii into SLSQP as x0. The rest of the solver stays unchanged.
backlog.title: Site-occupancy annealing on a candidate grid

backlog.spec: After the time loop in solve, take only the final best centres and radii and run one extra SLSQP call from them with maxiter 1000 and options ftol 1e-12 (passing the same pair and wall constraints). Keep the result only if the repaired sum of radii is larger than before. This is a single extra call that uses the time reserved by the 0.8 fraction, so lower TIME_FRACTION to 0.85 to keep the total under 30 s of CPU time.
backlog.title: Final tight polish of the incumbent

backlog.spec: Maintain an archive of distinct local optima found during the run. After each SLSQP and repair, compute a fingerprint of the packing: the sorted radii rounded to 0.01 together with the sorted list of contact counts. Store the packing if its fingerprint is new. Each basin-hopping step, with probability 0.3, start from a random archive member chosen with probability proportional to its novelty (distance in sorted-radius space to the nearest other member) rather than from the incumbent. Keep the incumbent logic as it is otherwise, so the archive only changes which parent is perturbed.
backlog.title: Novelty-archive restart selection

backlog.spec: Add a weak attraction term to the SLSQP objective that pulls each centre toward the centre of mass of the packing: objective = -sum(r) + lam * sum(|c_i - c_mean|^2), with lam = 0.002 for the first half of the iterations and lam = 0 for the second half (two SLSQP calls with the same constraints, the second warm-started from the first). The pull compacts the layout so that fewer circles end up as rattlers near the walls. Pass the gradient analytically in the objective function. Keep the pair and wall constraints unchanged.
backlog.title: Gravity-like centre pull regulariser

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, each step perturbs only one block: with probability 0.5 jitter the centres (sigma 0.02, radii copied from the incumbent as now), otherwise keep the centres fixed and jitter only the radii by N(0, 0.02) before calling _solve_once. In the radii-only case pass the centres unchanged and let SLSQP start with the incumbent's centres. Alternate the mode so that each block receives about half of the steps. This splits the perturbation space into two lower-dimensional moves that SLSQP can explore more finely.
backlog.title: Block-coordinate basin hopping

backlog.spec: Add a new basin-hopping move with probability 0.2 per step. Multiply all incumbent radii by a factor 0.97 and keep centres unchanged. Run _solve_once from this shrunken state (radii start small so SLSQP has room to move the centres apart). Then apply the usual repair. The move lets the packing loosen and reorganise around a fixed set of contact points, without the large centre jitter used by the current step. Only the move choice changes; the acceptance rule stays as it is.
backlog.title: Breathing move: shrink then regrow

backlog.spec: Each basin-hopping step, with probability 0.3, build a fresh centre set by uniform random sampling in [0.05, 0.95]^2. Compute the cost matrix between the n fresh centres and the n sorted-by-distance-to-centre slots of the incumbent (slot k is the incumbent's k-th circle by distance from its centre of mass). Use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment to match the incumbent's radii to fresh centres so that large radii go to centres far from the boundary. Use these matched radii and centres as the SLSQP start. The matching is one-off per step, so the cost is negligible compared with SLSQP.
backlog.title: Radius-profile transplant by assignment

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, replace the pair constraint sqrt(dx^2+dy^2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 with the polynomial form dx^2+dy^2 - (r_i+r_j)^2 >= 0, also requiring r_i+r_j >= 0 through the existing r>=0 constraint. The square-root gradient blows up when two centres nearly coincide, which happens often when radii grow, so the polynomial form should give SLSQP cleaner gradients. Keep the same constraint list and maxiter. Keep the final _repair step unchanged, so validity is still guaranteed.
backlog.title: Squared-distance pair constraints in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Before calling SLSQP, scale all centre coordinates and radii by s = sqrt(n) so that the decision variables are O(1) and the pair constraints have comparable magnitude. Unscale the result by dividing by s, and set the container limits to s and s-1 respectively. The objective and tolerances then act on well-conditioned quantities. This is a conditioning change only, so the search trajectory should stay about the same, but SLSQP's default ftol becomes relatively tighter for the packing scale. Apply it to both the first solve and the basin-hopping solves.
backlog.title: Rescale SLSQP variables to typical spacing

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping step, replace the Gaussian centre noise N(0, 0.02) with a heavy-tailed draw: for each circle, sample a Student-t or Cauchy perturbation with scale 0.01 and clip extreme values at 0.3. Most circles then move only slightly, but occasionally one moves far, which can escape a basin without destroying the whole packing. Keep the radius noise and _relocate as they are. The random draws must come from rng.
backlog.title: Heavy-tailed Levy-flight perturbations

backlog.spec: Track the incumbent value f* in basin hopping. After each SLSQP solve with value f, if f is below f* - 0.002, apply the stretching transform g = f + alpha*(f* - f)... in practice, define the acceptance score as f + 0.5*tanh(f - f*) so that a worse solution that is only slightly worse is not penalised too strongly, and accept the candidate when its score exceeds the incumbent's score under the same transform. Compare candidates using this stretched score, but always store the true best separately and return it. This is a single acceptance-rule change with no new moves.
backlog.title: Stretched-energy escape from plateaus

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that perturbs only one coordinate axis. With probability 0.3 per step, pick either x or y at random and add N(0, 0.03) noise to that coordinate for a random 30 percent subset of circles, leaving the other coordinate unchanged. Axis-aligned moves change which circles are in contact without disturbing the row structure of the packing in the other direction. Use the rng seed for all draws, and run the usual relocation and SLSQP afterwards.
backlog.title: Axis-only coordinate kick

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that applies a random affine map to the incumbent centres. Draw a 2x2 matrix A = I + N(0, 0.03) entries, centre the centres at 0.5, apply A, add 0.5 back, then clip to [0,1] and clip the radii so that they fit. This shear or stretch changes the relative spacing of the whole packing at once, which is a different kind of move from per-circle noise. With probability 0.5 use this move instead of the usual Gaussian kick, and keep the usual relocation and SLSQP afterwards.
backlog.title: Affine kick on the incumbent

backlog.spec: Keep the best two distinct packings found so far, and every 10 steps run a relinking step. Pick a random mixing parameter t in (0.2, 0.8), set the starting centres to (1-t)*A + t*B, where A and B are the centres of the two elites matched by nearest-index permutation after sorting by x coordinate, and set starting radii to the mean of the two radii. Run SLSQP from this start and keep the result only if it beats the incumbent. The step lies between two good basins, so it can find a new one without restarting from random points.
backlog.title: Path relinking between elite packings

backlog.spec: After _repair, add a deterministic growth pass. Repeat up to 5 sweeps: for each circle in random order, compute the largest radius it can take without overlapping any other circle or leaving the square, which is min over neighbours of (d_ij - r_j) and over the walls, and set its radius to that value if larger. The repair only shrinks radii, so this pass can recover slack left by the SLSQP tolerance and by the repair, with a feasibility check at the end. Apply it to every candidate before comparing sums of radii.
backlog.title: Greedy radius inflation sweep after repair

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with a clustered start. Draw k = round(sqrt(n)) cluster centres uniformly in [0.15, 0.85]^2, assign each circle to a cluster at random with probability proportional to a Dirichlet(1) weight, and place each circle at its cluster centre plus N(0, 0.08) noise, clipped into [0.05, 0.95]. Dense clusters separated by gaps give SLSQP a different initial contact pattern than the uniform start, and the rest of the search stays the same.
backlog.title: Cluster-centred initialisation

backlog.spec: Inside _solve_once, add the constraint r_i <= cap for all circles, where cap starts at 0.5 times the expected mean radius and is relaxed in two stages: solve with the cap, then re-solve with the cap raised to 1.0 and warm-start from the first result. Early capping stops a few large circles from locking into a poor configuration before the small circles have found their places. The final solve has no cap, so the output is the usual uncapped optimum. Apply to the first solve only.
backlog.title: Radius-cap curriculum in SLSQP

backlog.spec: Treat the packing as a decision problem. Bisect on a common radius r. For each r, minimise a penalty energy over centres only: the sum of squared overlap violations between pairs (max(0, 2r - d_ij)) plus squared wall violations, using L-BFGS-B with analytic gradients and a few random restarts seeded from rng. Take the largest r that reaches zero energy (within 1e-9), then use those centres as the x0 for the existing SLSQP call with radii set to r. Keep the existing basin-hopping loop and the repair step unchanged. This is a different route to the same local optima, which may land in different basins than radius-sum SLSQP.
backlog.title: Feasibility bisection on a common radius

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random first-start in _solve_once with a short molecular-dynamics style anneal. Use fixed target radii r_t = 0.12 scaled so the disks are dense. Treat overlaps as a harmonic soft repulsion energy and integrate overdamped Langevin dynamics for about 3000 steps with step size 1e-3. Lower the temperature geometrically from 1e-2 to 1e-5 over the run. Then pass the centres and radii to SLSQP. Everything is driven by the seed rng. The goal is a thermally equilibrated, low-stress start that SLSQP can refine into a better basin.
backlog.title: Langevin soft-disk annealing as the first start

backlog.spec: Remove the 4n wall constraints from the SLSQP problem by reparameterising centres as c = 0.5 + 0.5 * tanh(u) (or a logistic map) with u unconstrained. Keep radii bounded by requiring r_i <= min(c_i, 1 - c_i) through the same map, or keep it as a single inequality per circle. Map the optimised u back to centres and radii at the end, then run the existing _repair. Pair-distance constraints stay as they are. This changes the geometry SLSQP sees near walls and may let circles slide along the boundary more easily.
backlog.title: Sigmoid reparameterisation of centres

backlog.spec: Use scipy.optimize.least_squares (trust-region reflective, method='trf') instead of SLSQP for a stage of each solve. Residuals are the pairwise overlap violations, the wall violations, and a term -sqrt(w) * r_i for every circle, with w annealed from 0.01 to 1 across the stage. Variables are centres and radii. Finish with a short SLSQP polish on the active set. The least-squares solver handles the sparse residual structure differently from SLSQP's quadratic subproblems and may reach different local optima.
backlog.title: Penalty least-squares with annealed radius weight

backlog.spec: Build the first layout greedily by tangency. Start with one circle in the corner. For each next circle, enumerate the points tangent to two already-placed circles and to walls or other circles, using closed-form two-circle tangency. Score each candidate by the radius it could take without overlap, computed as the minimum of wall distance and gap to all placed circles. Keep the candidate with the largest radius, with a random tie-break from rng. Use these centres and radii as the x0 for _solve_once. This differs from random or best-candidate sampling because it builds contact structure directly.
backlog.title: Apollonian tangent insertion for the initial layout

backlog.spec: Add a regularisation term to the SLSQP objective: minimise -sum(r) - t * sum(log r_i), where t is annealed from 0.05 to 0 across the SLSQP stage, applied as separate calls with t stepped down. This keeps all radii strictly positive during early iterations, so small circles are not pushed to zero and frozen out of the search. At t = 0 the problem is the original one. The incumbent logic and repair are unchanged. This is an entropy-like pull on small circles, distinct from a hard floor.
backlog.title: Log-barrier on radii annealed to zero

backlog.spec: Add a new perturbation move to the basin-hopping loop, chosen with probability 0.25 per step. Pick one wall at random. For circles whose centre lies within 0.15 of that wall, reflect the centre across the wall line so it lands just outside the square, then clip it back into the square. Radii are scaled down by 0.8 for the reflected circles. Follow with _relocate as usual and run SLSQP. The move makes a large, structured jump near the boundary, which the Gaussian kick never does. It is a bolder, topology-changing move.
backlog.title: Mirror-image wall kick in basin hopping

backlog.spec: Before the main SLSQP solve, optimise a homotopy of objectives F_p = sum(r_i^p) with p ramped from 0.5 to 1 in three stages, each a separate SLSQP run from the previous result. Lower p favours spreading radii more evenly, which can avoid early commitment to a bad basin. Keep the final stage at p = 1 so the target matches the existing objective. Apply the homotopy only to the first start, leaving basin hopping unchanged. Use the same constraints throughout.
backlog.title: Power-mean homotopy on the objective

backlog.spec: Build the first layout by splitting the square into a 2 by 2 grid of quadrants. Assign circles to quadrants in proportion to a random split of n. Solve each quadrant as a small packing scaled into its cell using a short SLSQP run, with the cell as the square, then stitch the four results into the full square and run SLSQP on all circles with the stitched centres as x0. Repair then runs as normal. This is coarse-to-fine decomposition at the level of the whole start, and it gives the global optimiser structure at quadrant scale.
backlog.title: Quadrant-split coarse-to-fine start

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve, count for every circle how many other circles or walls are within 1e-4 of contact. Circles with few contacts are rattlers and carry no stress. Use this count as a per-circle noise scale: the perturbation sigma for circle i is 0.02 * (1 + c_i) / (1 + max c) instead of a constant 0.02. Apply it to the centres and radii in the basin-hopping kick. Fully-constrained circles then move little and the search focuses on loose parts of the packing. Keep everything else unchanged.
backlog.title: Stress-weighted kick with contact-count scaling

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when x0 is None, replace the uniform random centres with a row-based layout. Draw k uniformly from {4,5,6,7}, split n circles into k rows with random counts that sum to n, and place each row at a height evenly spaced in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]. Within a row, space centres evenly along x with small uniform jitter (about 0.02) and a random horizontal offset per row. Set initial radii to about 0.4 times the row spacing. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged. Use rng for every draw so the seed still controls the run.
backlog.title: Row-strip layout start

backlog.spec: After each SLSQP solve in basin hopping, estimate the Lagrange multipliers of the pair and wall constraints by a non-negative least-squares fit of the objective gradient onto the active constraint Jacobian at the solution. Mark constraints whose multiplier is about zero as inactive. Re-solve SLSQP once with only the constraints that have a non-zero multiplier or an actual contact (gap below 1e-6), then check the full constraint set and keep the result only if it is feasible. Otherwise keep the original solve. This differs from distance-based pair pruning because it uses the dual solution.
backlog.title: KKT-multiplier constraint pruning

backlog.spec: Replace the fixed 0.02 Gaussian kick in basin hopping with a choice among four kick scales {0.005, 0.01, 0.02, 0.05}. Keep a Beta(successes+1, failures+1) posterior for each scale, where a success means the repaired candidate sum beats the incumbent. Each step draw one sample from each posterior with rng, use the scale with the largest sample, and update its counts after the solve. This is a bandit over step sizes; no schedule is assumed.
backlog.title: Thompson-sampled kick scale

backlog.spec: Before the first SLSQP solve in _solve_once, run about 200 sweeps of an alternating projection. Each sweep sets every circle's radius to the largest value that fits its current position (min of wall clearance and half the nearest-neighbour gap, using a KD-tree or the full distance matrix). Then for each overlapping pair, move both centres apart along their connecting line by half the overlap, clipped to [0,1]. Stop when the total overlap is below 1e-4. Pass the resulting centres and radii as x0 to SLSQP. Vectorise each sweep with numpy.
backlog.title: Alternating-projection feasibility sweeps

backlog.spec: Replace the random first start with a force-directed relaxation. Place circles uniformly at random in the square. Give every pair a spring with rest length equal to 1.6 times the sum of their current radii, which start at 0.06, and a soft wall repulsion. Run 400 gradient steps of overdamped motion with a step size that cools linearly to zero. Radii then grow each step toward the local clearance, capped at the wall and neighbour gaps. Finally pass centres and radii to SLSQP as x0. This is a physical start, not a grid.
backlog.title: Hooke spring relaxation start

backlog.spec: Before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, perform m=40 Gibbs sweeps on the incumbent with the energy E = -sum of the feasible radii. For a chosen circle, sample a candidate centre uniformly in the square, compute its feasible radius from the wall distances and the nearest-neighbour gap, and accept it with the Metropolis rule at temperature T=0.002, which decays by 0.9 per sweep. Keep the state with the best energy, then polish it with SLSQP. This differs from the greedy relocation of the smallest circle because the move is stochastic and applies to any circle.
backlog.title: Low-temperature Gibbs circle resampling

backlog.spec: Speed up _repair so more basin-hopping steps fit in the 24 s budget. Use scipy.spatial.cKDTree to find each circle's neighbours within 2*max(r)+0.05, and compute the overlap only for those pairs. Loop over violating pairs in order of overlap, scaling both radii by the same factor as now, and stop as soon as no pair violates. Keep the SHRINK margin and the final tolerance check identical. The output must remain exactly feasible under the 1e-10 harness check. The goal is only a faster repair, with the same results as before.
backlog.title: Vectorised spatial-hash repair

backlog.spec: In basin hopping, accept a candidate only after a robustness check. Run SLSQP twice from the same perturbed candidate with two independent draws of 0.005 jitter on the centres (use rng), repair both, and score the candidate by the minimum of the two repaired sums. Accept it into the incumbent only if this minimum beats the incumbent's repaired sum. This trades iterations for fewer false improvements from lucky SLSQP convergence, which matters given the noise sd of 0.0034.
backlog.title: Robust two-start acceptance

backlog.spec: In _solve_once with no x0, solve first with n+3 circles in the optimisation, where the last 3 are phantoms. Phantoms are present in all pair and wall constraints but carry zero weight in the objective, so they only push neighbours apart and absorb space. After the solve, delete the phantoms, keep the n largest-radius circles, and run SLSQP again on the n-circle problem from that state. Sum radii are computed only over the real circles. This is a different use of the spare-circle idea from growing or shrinking the count.
backlog.title: Phantom-circle density start

backlog.spec: Add a basin-hopping move that picks a random line through the square (horizontal, vertical or diagonal) and mirrors a random subset of about 4 circles across it to produce new centres that are close to their reflections. Blend the mirrored centres with the originals at a random mix in [0.3, 0.7]. Then continue with the usual relocation and SLSQP solve. The move does not require a symmetric final packing; it only proposes correlated configurations that the continuous optimiser then refines.
backlog.title: Mirror-symmetric pair kick

backlog.spec: For the first SLSQP start only, solve in a rectangle of width W=1+d and height H=1-d with d drawn uniformly from [-0.04, 0.04] (area preserved). Use the same pair and wall constraints with the rectangle bounds, then affinely rescale the centres to the unit square (x/W, y/H, radii scaled by min(1/W, 1/H)) before the existing clip and repair. Keep basin hopping unchanged afterwards. This tests whether a different container shape steers the first basin into a better region.
backlog.title: Anisotropic container relaxation start

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when called from basin hopping, first identify circles whose wall gap is below 1e-3 in the incumbent. Run SLSQP with those circles' centres held fixed (bounds collapsed to their current values) and maxiter 60. Then run the normal SLSQP with all variables free, starting from that output. The pinned stage fixes the rigid wall frame while the interior reorganises, and the free stage then lets the wall contacts release. No new hyperparameters beyond the 60-iteration cap.
backlog.title: Boundary-pinned staged release

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with three independent chains, each seeded from its own random start with rng children derived from the seed. Every 10 basin-hopping steps, each island sends its best packing to the next island in a ring, where it replaces that island's incumbent only if its repaired sum is larger. The final answer is the best packing across islands. The time accounting stays on process time with the same TIME_FRACTION. This is a coarse island-model variant of replica exchange, with migration on a fixed schedule rather than Metropolis swaps.
backlog.title: Three-island ring migration

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping perturbation, replace the isotropic Gaussian kick on all 3n variables with a kick confined to a random k-dimensional subspace, k=8. Draw an 8 by 3n Gaussian matrix each step, orthonormalise its rows via QR, and set the kick to a sigma-scaled random combination of those rows (sigma 0.02). Keep the centre clip and repair. This concentrates the search on a few collective displacement modes, which differs from the per-coordinate kicks tried so far.
backlog.title: Random-subspace kick

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, on each SLSQP call, drop each non-near pair constraint with probability 0.3, where near means centre distance below the sum of current radii plus 0.15. Always keep near pairs and all wall constraints. This gives a cheaper, more exploratory local solve that may step across small barriers. The final output is still checked by the existing _repair step, so validity is unchanged. Use the rng to make the dropout reproducible.
backlog.title: Stochastic pair-constraint dropout during SLSQP

backlog.spec: Make the basin-hopping loop two-level. An outer step applies a coarse move: relocate three randomly chosen circles with _relocate and then run one SLSQP. An inner loop then runs 15 small-kick basin-hopping steps (sigma 0.01) on the result, accepting the inner best only if it beats the incumbent. Outer steps repeat until the time budget is spent. The coarse moves explore topology changes and the inner loop does the fine local search, which is a nested two-scale architecture.
backlog.title: Nested two-level basin hopping

backlog.spec: Keep the top four distinct packings from the search. For a new start, take two of them at random, apply each of the 8 symmetries of the unit square to the second, and match circles to the first by minimum total centre distance with scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment. Average the matched centres and radii, then use the averaged configuration as the x0 of one SLSQP solve (with a small jitter from rng). Keep the current basin hopping for the other steps. This recombines structure across elite packings instead of perturbing a single one.
backlog.title: Procrustes consensus crossover of elite packings

backlog.spec: Add a perturbation that rigidly rotates the whole incumbent packing about the centre (0.5, 0.5) by a random angle uniform in [-0.05, 0.05] radians, with probability 0.2 per basin-hopping step. Clip the rotated centres to the square, shrink any radius that now violates a wall through the existing repair, and then run the normal SLSQP. Rotation preserves all pairwise geometry, so it changes which circles touch the walls without destroying the local contact network.
backlog.title: Global rigid rotation kick

backlog.spec: Before each SLSQP solve in basin hopping, take 30 leapfrog-based HMC steps on the energy E = sum over pairs of max(0, r_i + r_j - d_ij)^2 plus wall penalties, with radii fixed at the incumbent values plus 0.01. Use step size 0.01, unit mass, and a temperature chosen so that acceptance is about 0.6. Pass the final configuration to SLSQP as x0. Gradients are analytic and cheap for n=32. This is a sampling-based kick that moves through soft-overlap configurations rather than adding a random Gaussian.
backlog.title: Hamiltonian Monte Carlo sampling of a soft-overlap energy

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with a population of 12 walkers, all starting from the first SLSQP solution. Use an inverse-temperature schedule beta that rises geometrically from 1 to 50 over the time budget. At each generation, weight each walker by exp(beta times the change in repaired radius sum since the last generation), resample the walkers with systematic resampling, perturb each with the existing Gaussian kick and relocation, and run one SLSQP and repair per walker. The output is the best walker seen. This extends the single-chain Metropolis attempts into a population-based anneal.
backlog.title: Population annealing with weight resampling

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, optimise unconstrained variables u and map each centre coordinate through a triangle-wave fold, x = 1 - |1 - (u mod 2)|, so every centre stays in [0, 1] without any wall inequalities. Radii keep their own bound r >= 0 through SLSQP bounds, and the wall-clearance terms are removed from cons. The fold makes the objective piecewise smooth, so keep the pair-distance constraints smooth. After SLSQP, map the folded centres back, then clip and run _repair as before. This shrinks the constraint count from about 4n + n(n-1)/2 to roughly n(n-1)/2 + n, which may allow more SLSQP iterations per second inside the time budget.
backlog.title: Folded-coordinate walls instead of wall constraints

backlog.spec: Add a penalty lambda * sum_i (r_i - mean(r))^2 to the SLSQP objective, where the objective is -sum(r) + lambda * variance term. Set lambda at the start of each basin-hopping step to 0.5 * (best radius spread), then decay it geometrically to zero over the SLSQP call's iterations (for example, run three SLSQP passes with lambda = 0.1, 0.01, 0 from the same start). The idea is to push the optimiser away from lopsided radius patterns that trap it, then release the constraint so the final stage optimises the true sum. Keep the final pass with lambda = 0 so the reported objective is unchanged.
backlog.title: Annealed equal-radius pull regulariser

backlog.spec: Maintain a small elite set of the top 5 distinct packings found so far. For each new start, pick one elite packing at random, then sample a fresh centre set by taking each elite centre and adding Gaussian noise with a standard deviation equal to 0.3 times the mean nearest-neighbour distance, then clip to the square. Radii start from the elite radii shifted by the same noise. This is an estimation-of-distribution step over packing structure rather than a pure kick on the incumbent, and it fills the role of the first random start once the elite set has at least two members. Use the seed for every draw.
backlog.title: Elite-density sampled starts

backlog.spec: Re-express each centre as a polar offset (rho_i, theta_i) from the square's centre (0.5, 0.5), with rho_i in [0, 0.71] and theta_i in [0, 2 pi). Initialise rho uniformly in the disk and theta uniformly on the circle. Feed the Cartesian coordinates 0.5 + rho cos theta and 0.5 + rho sin theta into the existing pair and wall constraints, so SLSQP still sees the same geometry but optimises in polar variables. Map back after SLSQP and keep the existing clip and _repair steps. This changes the local basin structure near the boundary and is cheap to implement inside _solve_once.
backlog.title: Polar-coordinate centre parametrisation

backlog.spec: Replace the Gaussian centre kick in basin hopping with a kick on the pairwise distance matrix. Compute the incumbent's distance matrix D, multiply each off-diagonal entry by an independent factor exp(N(0, sigma)) with sigma = 0.02, symmetrise, and recover centres with classical multidimensional scaling (top-two eigenvectors of the double-centred matrix). Use the recovered centres as the SLSQP start with the incumbent radii, then apply the usual relocation and repair. Rotations and reflections in the MDS output are harmless because SLSQP only sees the geometry, so the kick is rotation-invariant by construction.
backlog.title: Distance-matrix kick in pair space

backlog.spec: Keep two perturbation scales, a fast scale of 0.02 and a slow scale of 0.005, and choose between them by a rolling success count over the last 10 steps. When the fast scale has produced no improvement in 10 consecutive steps, switch the next 10 steps to the slow scale, and switch back on any improvement. Only the choice of sigma changes; the SLSQP, relocation and repair steps stay the same. This is a schedule over the kick magnitude, separate from the annealed and Thompson-sampled variants already tried, and it needs only a counter and two constants.
backlog.title: Two-timescale kick scale with stagnation counter

backlog.spec: For each basin-hopping candidate, run the perturb-and-solve step twice from two independent kicks of the same incumbent, then accept the candidate only if the average of its two repaired sums beats the incumbent's repaired sum. Store the candidate with the higher repaired sum as the new best when accepted. The goal is to cut false accepts caused by lucky SLSQP convergence. Costs twice the solves per step, so compare per-time results against the incumbent under equal CPU time.
backlog.title: Bootstrap-averaged acceptance test

backlog.spec: After each repair, compute for every circle its slack s_i = min over neighbours j of (d_ij - r_i - r_j), together with the wall clearance. Pick the circle with the largest slack and the circle with the smallest slack, transfer a fraction 0.1 of the smaller circle's slack-limited radius to the larger one, then re-run _repair and a short SLSQP with maxiter 30 starting from that state. Accept the result only if the repaired sum improves. This is a local radius-exchange move that targets rattlers and loose contacts, and it is distinct from the radius swap and LP polish moves already tried.
backlog.title: Gap-equalising radius reassignment

backlog.spec: Build a random geometric graph on n nodes with edges between pairs whose random initial positions are closer than 0.25, compute the Fiedler-style embedding from the two smallest non-trivial eigenvectors of its graph Laplacian, rescale the embedding to fit [0.05, 0.95]^2, and use it as the centre start in _solve_once with equal radii 0.05. For the spectral step use numpy.linalg.eigh on the dense Laplacian (n = 32 is tiny). Different seeds then give different embeddings. This replaces the uniform random initial centres for the first SLSQP solve only, and the basin hopping loop is unchanged.
backlog.title: Spectral start from the Laplacian of a random geometric graph

backlog.spec: Replace the objective -sum(r) in _solve_once with a smooth surrogate: minimise -sum(r) + mu * sum over pairs of max(0, overlap)^2 computed by the existing pair constraint values, where mu starts at 0 and is raised to 100 over the SLSQP call. Enforce hard feasibility only at the last SLSQP pass, which keeps the constraint set but relaxes the early iterations. The aim is to take larger early steps through the feasible-free region, then tighten. Compare against the existing SLSQP-only path under equal CPU time.
backlog.title: Bounded-gradient step inside SLSQP via sum-of-squares objective

backlog.spec: Before each basin-hopping SLSQP call, perturb the candidate centres by running about 30 L-BFGS-B iterations on an inverse-square repulsion energy E = sum over pairs of 1/(d_ij^2 + 1e-6) plus a matching wall term 1/(dist_to_wall^2 + 1e-6), with all centres kept inside [0,1]^2 by bounds. The energy weight starts at 1e-4 times the mean squared radius and decays geometrically to zero over the optimiser calls, so the pre-spread only pushes overlapping pairs apart and does not change the local optimum that SLSQP finally reaches. Radii are untouched. Use the seeded rng for any initial jitter and keep the existing relocation and repair steps unchanged.
backlog.title: Coulomb pre-spread before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve

backlog.spec: Replace the uniform random first-start centres in _solve_once with a combinatorial site assignment. Build a triangular lattice with spacing chosen so that about 1.3n sites fall inside the unit square, rotate it by a random angle drawn from the seeded rng, and offset it by a random shift. Keep the sites nearest to the square centre, then use scipy.optimize.linear_sum_assignment between n random target points and these sites, with cost equal to the squared distance, to pick n distinct sites. Use the chosen sites as the initial centres and give all radii the value 0.05. This is an assignment-based start with an explicit lattice prior, which is different from the earlier lattice-perturbed start that did not use assignment.
backlog.title: Assignment-matched rotated triangular-lattice start

backlog.spec: Insert a cheap non-SLSQP stage before the first SLSQP solve only. Minimise the penalty f(c,r) = -sum r + mu * sum of squared positive parts of pair overlaps and wall violations, with mu = 10, using a Barzilai-Borwein spectral projected gradient with a nonmonotone line search written in numpy, for at most 300 iterations and projected onto the box [0,1] for the centres and [0,0.5] for the radii. Stop early when the maximum violation is below 1e-4. Pass the result to SLSQP as x0. The step is O(n^2) per iteration in numpy and needs no new packages. Keep the rest of the pipeline as it is.
backlog.title: Spectral-gradient penalty pre-optimiser

backlog.spec: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with a population of 6 independent chains, each started from its own _solve_once result with a different rng child stream (use rng.spawn or distinct seeds derived from the seed argument). Split the time budget into 4 epochs of equal CPU time. At the end of each epoch rank the chains by repaired radius sum, drop the worst 3, and clone the best 3 with their incumbent copied in. Run basin-hopping steps within each chain as before. Return the best chain at the end. Use only seeded randomness. The point is to spend budget on the chains that are doing well instead of spreading it evenly across restarts.
backlog.title: Epoch culling of independent chains

backlog.spec: Before the SLSQP call in _solve_once, run a short method of multipliers. Keep a vector of multipliers lambda for the pair and wall constraints, initialised to zero. Repeat 4 times: minimise the augmented Lagrangian -sum r + sum of (max(0, lambda_k/rho + g_k(c,r))^2 - (lambda_k/rho)^2) * rho/2 over the centres and radii with L-BFGS-B, then update lambda_k = max(0, lambda_k + rho*g_k) with rho = 20. Use only the final (c, r) as the x0 handed to SLSQP. The active-set information then enters the warm start, not just the penalty as in earlier continuation attempts. Keep the pair-constraint list and repair step unchanged.
backlog.title: Method of multipliers with a shifted squared penalty

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, for the first 50 SLSQP iterations, pass only a random subset of the pair constraints, keeping each pair with probability 0.5 and always keeping pairs whose centre distance is below r_i + r_j + 0.1 at the start point. After those iterations, restart SLSQP from its current iterate with the full pair set and the remaining iteration budget. Drawing the subset from the seeded rng keeps runs reproducible. The aim is a cheaper early phase, where the feasible region is large and most pairs are far from active, followed by a full-constraint refinement.
backlog.title: Stochastic pair-constraint dropout in the early SLSQP iterations

backlog.spec: Add a start that is a clipped hexagonal packing. Choose a hex spacing so that a rotated lattice contains more than n points in the unit square, with the rotation angle and the lattice offset both drawn from the seeded rng. Keep the n points with the largest clearance from the walls and from each other, then run SLSQP from them with all radii set to half the nearest-neighbour distance. Use this start on the first SLSQP call only, with the random uniform start kept for the basin-hopping calls. Do not hard-code any coordinates; the lattice is generated by formula.
backlog.title: Hex-lattice clip with random orientation and vacancy removal

backlog.spec: In the basin-hopping loop, before each SLSQP call draw a single cap value M from a log-uniform distribution on [0.12, 0.5] and add the constraint r_i <= M to the SLSQP inequality set for that call only. A small cap forces the optimiser to spread mass to other circles, which can open a different contact pattern, while the large caps leave the problem unchanged. Keep the best incumbent rule as it is and apply the cap only inside _solve_once. This is a cheap, reversible regulariser that can be switched off by setting the range to a single large value.
backlog.title: Radius-cap jitter with per-step sampling

backlog.spec: After SLSQP in each basin-hopping step, run a short Levenberg-Marquardt pass with scipy.optimize.least_squares (method 'lm' is not allowed for bounded problems, so use method 'trf' with x_scale set to 0.01) on the residual vector made of the active pair overlaps and the active wall violations, with the target radii fixed at the SLSQP solution plus 1e-4. Accept the result only if the repaired radius sum improves. This tightens the contact network to machine precision in a fraction of the time SLSQP needs and gives the final polish a different stopping rule from the current SLSQP tolerance.
backlog.title: Bounded-step Levenberg-Marquardt on the contact residuals

backlog.spec: Replace the wall inequality constraints by a reparameterisation. Let the optimiser work on unbounded variables u, with c = sigmoid(u) mapped into the open square, rescaled to [r_min, 1 - r_min] with r_min = 1e-3, and keep the radii as they are. The wall constraints then vanish from the SLSQP constraint vector, which shortens it by 4n, and the chain rule is a diagonal Jacobian computed by hand. Map back to centres after the solve, clip to [0,1], and run the existing repair. Use the same seeded initial centres mapped through the inverse sigmoid. Keep the pair constraints as they are.
backlog.title: Sigmoid-bounded centre parametrisation inside SLSQP

cand.description: Replace the single basin-hopping chain with 6 independent chains (own seeded rng streams), run in 4 equal CPU-time epochs, and at the end of each epoch keep the best 3 chains and clone them over the worst 3; return the best chain.

incumbent.description: Before each basin-hopping SLSQP solve, move the smallest-radius circle to the best of 30 random centres, scored by the local sum of radii after setting its radius to the largest non-overlapping value.
